title: BBC Learning English from the News 2024 — Quiz 6
description: Choose the best answer for each question about vocabulary and usage.

elements.name: q51_turn_the_tide
elements.title: Vacancies had been increasing for years until new businesses began to turn the tide. What did the businesses help do?
choices: Speed up the trend
Measure the trend
Reverse the trend
Hide the trend

elements.name: q52_snappy
elements.title: An editor asks for a snappy opening paragraph. What kind of paragraph do they want?
choices: Brief and engaging
Slow and repetitive
Long and highly detailed
Formal and cautious

elements.name: q53_quick_fire
elements.title: The interviewer fired off a series of quick-fire questions. How did the questions come?
choices: In several languages
In rapid succession
With long breaks between them
In order of difficulty

elements.name: q54_back_and_forth
elements.title: The children passed the ball back and forth. How did the ball move?
choices: From one child to another and back again
In a straight line away from both children
Around the room in a single direction
Upward without being caught
elements.correctAnswer: From one child to another and back again

elements.name: q55_carve_out_a_bigger_slice
elements.title: A small business worked hard to carve out a bigger slice of the market. What was its aim?
choices: Reduce the total size of the market
Win a larger share of sales
Exit the market quietly
Keep its existing share unchanged
elements.correctAnswer: Win a larger share of sales

elements.name: q56_biding_its_time
elements.title: The company is biding its time before announcing the product. What is it doing?
choices: Trying to forget its original plan
Making a decision by chance
Waiting patiently for the right moment
Rushing to announce before a rival
elements.correctAnswer: Waiting patiently for the right moment

elements.name: q57_gets_a_greenish_light
elements.title: The proposal gets a greenish light from the committee. What does the playful phrase suggest?
choices: It receives unconditional approval.
It is unanimously rejected.
It receives some approval, with reservations.
It has not yet been discussed.
elements.correctAnswer: It receives some approval, with reservations.

elements.name: q58_dissolve_parliament
elements.title: What happens when a country dissolves parliament ahead of an election?
choices: It appoints one extra member of parliament.
It formally brings the current parliament to an end.
It extends the current parliament's term.
It changes the location of parliament.
elements.correctAnswer: It formally brings the current parliament to an end.

elements.name: q59_a_dangerous_vacuum
elements.title: The leader resigned suddenly, leaving a dangerous vacuum. What does that phrase refer to?
choices: A temporary shortage of office space
A peaceful transfer of power
A lack of public interest in the news
A lack of leadership that could lead to conflict
elements.correctAnswer: A lack of leadership that could lead to conflict

elements.name: q60_tainted_legacy
elements.title: The scandal left the mayor with a tainted legacy. What does the phrase imply?
choices: The scandal damaged how the mayor would be remembered.
The mayor left money to the city.
The mayor's achievements would be forgotten entirely.
The mayor inherited a legal claim.
elements.correctAnswer: The scandal damaged how the mayor would be remembered.
